questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two charged spherical conductors of radius $R_1$ and $R_2$ are connected by a wire. Then the ratio of surface charge densities of the spheres $\left(\frac{\sigma_1}{\sigma_2}\right)$ is
questions.solution_text: When two conductors are connected by a wire, they reach the same potential: $V_1 = V_2$. So $\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{Q_1}{R_1} = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{Q_2}{R_2}$, giving $Q_1 R_2 = Q_2 R_1$. Surface charge density $\sigma = \frac{Q}{4\pi R^2}$, so $\sigma_1 R_1^2 = \sigma_2 R_2^2 \cdot \frac{R_1}{R_2}$. Using equal potentials: $\sigma_1 R_1 = \sigma_2 R_2$, hence $\frac{\sigma_1}{\sigma_2} = \frac{R_2}{R_1}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The velocity of a small ball of mass $M$ and density $d$, when dropped in a container filled with glycerine becomes constant after some time. If the density of glycerine is $\dfrac{d}{2}$, then the viscous force acting on the ball will be
questions.solution_text: At terminal velocity, $a = 0$, so $Mg = F_B + F_v$. Buoyant force $F_B = \frac{d}{2} \cdot V \cdot g$ where $M = dVg$, so $F_B = \frac{M}{2}g$. Therefore $F_v = Mg - F_B = Mg - \frac{Mg}{2} = \frac{Mg}{2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Force on Moving Charge in Magnetic Field
questions.question_text: An infinitely long straight conductor carries a current of 5 A as shown. An electron is moving with a speed of $10^5$ m/s parallel to the conductor. The perpendicular distance between the electron and the conductor is 20 cm at an instant. Calculate the magnitude of the force experienced by the electron at that instant.
questions.solution_text: Magnetic field due to current-carrying wire: $B = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{2I}{r} = \frac{10^{-7} \times 2 \times 5}{20 \times 10^{-2}} = \frac{1}{2} \times 10^{-5}$ T. Force on electron: $|F| = qvB = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 10^5 \times \frac{1}{2} \times 10^{-5} = 0.8 \times 10^{-19} = 8 \times 10^{-20}$ N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A dipole is placed in an electric field as shown. In which direction will it move?

options.text: Towards the left as its potential energy will increase.
Towards the right as its potential energy will decrease.
Towards the left as its potential energy will decrease.
Towards the right as its potential energy will increase.

questions.solution_text: Potential energy of electric dipole in external field $U = -\vec{P}\cdot\vec{E} = -PE\cos\theta$. The angle between $\vec{P}$ and $\vec{E}$ is 180°, so $U = +PE$. Moving towards the right decreases $E$ (non-uniform field), thus decreasing $U$. Net force on dipole is towards right, net torque is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A lens of large focal length and large aperture is best suited as an objective of an astronomical telescope since

options.text: A large aperture contributes to the quality and visibility of the images.
A large area of the objective ensures better light gathering power.
A large aperture provides a better resolution.

questions.solution_text: A large aperture objective lens in astronomical telescope: (1) increases light gathering power enabling observation of fainter objects, (2) improves resolving power (ability to observe two objects distinctly), and (3) contributes to quality and visibility of images. Hence all options are correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A screw gauge gives the following readings when used to measure the diameter of a wire: Main scale reading: 0 mm, Circular scale reading: 52 divisions. Given that 1 mm on main scale corresponds to 100 divisions on the circular scale. The diameter of the wire from the above data is
questions.solution_text: Pitch $P = 1$ mm, Number of circular divisions $n = 100$. Least count $LC = \frac{P}{n} = \frac{1}{100} = 0.01$ mm $= 0.001$ cm. Diameter $= MSR + (CSR \times LC) = 0 + (52 \times 0.001) = 0.052$ cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A nucleus with mass number 240 breaks into two fragments each of mass number 120, the binding energy per nucleon of unfragmented nuclei is 7.6 MeV while that of fragments is 8.5 MeV. The total gain in the Binding Energy in the process is
questions.solution_text: Total gain in $BE = (BE)_{products} - (BE)_{reactant} = [120 + 120] \times 8.5 - [240] \times 7.6 = 240 \times 8.5 - 240 \times 7.6 = 2040 - 1824 = 216$ MeV.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A small block slides down on a smooth inclined plane, starting from rest at time $t = 0$. Let $S_n$ be the distance travelled by the block in the interval $t = n-1$ to $t = n$. Then, the ratio $\dfrac{S_n}{S_{n+1}}$ is
questions.solution_text: Distance in $n$th second: $S_n = u + \frac{a}{2}(2n-1)$. With $u = 0$ and $a = g\sin\theta$: $S_n = \frac{g\sin\theta}{2}(2n-1)$ and $S_{n+1} = \frac{g\sin\theta}{2}(2n+1)$. Therefore $\frac{S_n}{S_{n+1}} = \frac{2n-1}{2n+1}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Find the value of the angle of emergence from the prism. Refractive index of the glass is $\sqrt{3}$. (Prism angle shown is 60°)
questions.solution_text: At point P, using Snell's law: $\frac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \frac{\mu_{air}}{\mu_{prism}}$. The angle of incidence inside the prism at emergence face is 30°. $\frac{\sin 30°}{\sin e} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, so $\sin e = \sqrt{3} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, giving $e = 60°$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A spring is stretched by 5 cm by a force 10 N. The time period of the oscillations when a mass of 2 kg is suspended by it is
questions.solution_text: Spring constant: $kx = F \Rightarrow k(5 \times 10^{-2}) = 10 \Rightarrow k = 200$ N/m. Time period: $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{m}{k}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{2}{200}} = 2\pi \times \frac{1}{10} = \frac{2\pi}{10} = 0.628$ s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A convex lens 'A' of focal length 20 cm and a concave lens 'B' of focal length 5 cm are kept along the same axis with a distance 'd' between them. If a parallel beam of light falling on 'A' leaves 'B' as a parallel beam, then the distance 'd' in cm will be
questions.solution_text: Parallel beam from convex lens converges at its focus (20 cm). For the beam to emerge parallel from concave lens, the rays must appear to diverge from the focus of the concave lens. So the image from the convex lens must fall at the focus of the concave lens. $d = f_A - f_B = 20 - 5 = 15$ cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
Column-I gives certain physical terms associated with flow of current through a metallic conductor. Column-II gives some mathematical relations involving electrical quantities. Match Column-I and Column-II with appropriate relations.

Column-I: (A) Drift Velocity, (B) Electrical Resistivity, (C) Relaxation Period, (D) Current Density
Column-II: (P) $\dfrac{m}{ne^2\rho}$, (Q) $nev_d$, (R) $\dfrac{eE\tau}{m}$, (S) $\dfrac{E}{J}$
questions.solution_text: Drift velocity $v_d = \frac{eE\tau}{m}$ → (R). Electrical resistivity $\rho = \frac{E}{J}$ → (S). Relaxation period $\tau = \frac{m}{ne^2\rho}$ → (P). Current density $J = \frac{I}{A} = nev_d$ → (Q). Match: (A)-(R), (B)-(S), (C)-(P), (D)-(Q).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The electron concentration in an $n$-type semiconductor is the same as hole concentration in a $p$-type semiconductor. An external field (electric) is applied across each of them. Compare the currents in them.

options.text: No current will flow in $p$-type, current will only flow in $n$-type

questions.solution_text: Current $I = neAv_d = neA\mu E$. Given $n_e = n_h$, so $\frac{I_n}{I_p} = \frac{n_e e A \mu_e E}{n_h e A \mu_h E} = \frac{\mu_e}{\mu_h}$. Since mobility of electrons $\mu_e > \mu_h$ (mobility of holes), $I_n > I_p$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A radioactive nucleus ${}^A_Z X$ undergoes spontaneous decay in the sequence ${}^A_Z X \rightarrow {}_{Z-1} B \rightarrow {}_{Z-3} C \rightarrow {}_{Z-2} D$, where $Z$ is the atomic number of element $X$. The possible decay particles in the sequence are
questions.solution_text: From $Z$ to $Z-1$: atomic number decreases by 1 → $\beta^+$ decay. From $Z-1$ to $Z-3$: atomic number decreases by 2 → $\alpha$ decay. From $Z-3$ to $Z-2$: atomic number increases by 1 → $\beta^-$ decay. Correct order: $\beta^+, \alpha, \beta^-$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Water falls from a height of 60 m at the rate of 15 kg/s to operate a turbine. The losses due to frictional force are 10% of the input energy. How much power is generated by the turbine? ($g = 10$ m/s²)
questions.solution_text: Incident power on turbine $= gh\frac{dm}{dt} = 10 \times 60 \times 15 = 9000$ W. Losses are 10%, so power generated $= \left(1 - \frac{10}{100}\right) \times 9000 = 0.9 \times 9000 = 8100$ W $= 8.1$ kW.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question_text: The number of photons per second on an average emitted by the source of monochromatic light of wavelength 600 nm, when it delivers the power of $3.3 \times 10^{-3}$ watt will be ($h = 6.6 \times 10^{-34}$ J s)
questions.solution_text: Power $P = \frac{n}{t} \cdot \frac{hc}{\lambda}$. So $\frac{n}{t} = \frac{P\lambda}{hc} = \frac{3.3 \times 10^{-3} \times 600 \times 10^{-9}}{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8} = \frac{3.3 \times 10^{-3} \times 6 \times 10^{-7}}{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8} = 10^{16}$ photons per second.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Direction of E and B Fields
questions.question_text: For a plane electromagnetic wave propagating in $x$-direction, which one of the following combination gives the correct possible directions for electric field ($E$) and magnetic field ($B$) respectively?
questions.solution_text: Direction of propagation of EM wave is along $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$. Given propagation along $x$-axis (i.e., $\hat{i}$). Checking option (2): $(-\hat{j}+\hat{k}) \times (-\hat{j}-\hat{k}) = (-\hat{j}+\hat{k}) \times (-\hat{j}-\hat{k}) = 2\hat{i}$ (along $x$). Hence option (2) is correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The effective resistance of a parallel connection that consists of four wires of equal length, equal area of cross-section and same material is 0.25 $\Omega$. What will be the effective resistance if they are connected in series?
questions.solution_text: In parallel: $R_P = \frac{R}{4} = 0.25\; \Omega$, so $R = 1\; \Omega$ (individual resistance). In series: $R_S = 4R = 4 \times 1 = 4\; \Omega$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a potentiometer circuit a cell of EMF 1.5 V gives balance point at 36 cm length of wire. If another cell of EMF 2.5 V replaces the first cell, then at what length of the wire, the balance point occurs?
questions.solution_text: Using potentiometer principle: $\frac{E_1}{E_2} = \frac{\ell_1}{\ell_2}$. So $\ell_2 = \ell_1 \times \frac{E_2}{E_1} = 36 \times \frac{2.5}{1.5} = 36 \times \frac{5}{3} = 60$ cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Polar molecules are the molecules

options.text: Acquire a dipole moment only in the presence of electric field due to displacement of charges
Acquire a dipole moment only when magnetic field is absent
Having a permanent electric dipole moment

questions.solution_text: In polar molecules, the centre of positive charges does not coincide with the centre of negative charges, giving them a permanent electric dipole moment of their own.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A parallel plate capacitor has a uniform electric field '$\vec{E}$' in the space between the plates. If the distance between the plates is '$d$' and the area of each plate is '$A$', the energy stored in the capacitor is ($\varepsilon_0$ = permittivity of free space)
questions.solution_text: Energy density $u = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2$. Total energy $U = u \times V = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2 \times Ad$ (since volume $V = Ad$ and $E$ is uniform).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The equivalent capacitance of the combination shown in the figure is (Three capacitors each of capacitance $C$ are shown in the circuit)
questions.solution_text: Points 1, 2, 3 are at the same potential (connected by conducting wire), so the middle capacitor is short-circuited and stores no charge. The circuit reduces to two capacitors $C$ in parallel: $C_{AB} = C + C = 2C$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements (A) and (B) and identify the correct answer.
(A) A zener diode is connected in reverse bias, when used as a voltage regulator.
(B) The potential barrier of $p$-$n$ junction lies between 0.1 V to 0.3 V.
questions.solution_text: Statement A is correct: Zener diode is connected in reverse bias as voltage regulator; voltage across it becomes constant after breakdown. Statement B is incorrect: The potential barrier of silicon $p$-$n$ junction is nearly 0.7 V, not 0.1–0.3 V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A particle is released from height $S$ from the surface of the Earth. At a certain height its kinetic energy is three times its potential energy. The height from the surface of earth and the speed of the particle at that instant are respectively
questions.solution_text: Let height above ground = $y$. Velocity after falling $(S-y)$: $v = \sqrt{2g(S-y)}$. $K = 3U$ gives $\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = 3mgy \Rightarrow m \cdot 2g(S-y) = 6mgy \Rightarrow S-y = 3y \Rightarrow y = \frac{S}{4}$. Speed $v = \sqrt{2g(S - \frac{S}{4})} = \sqrt{2g \cdot \frac{3S}{4}} = \sqrt{\frac{3gS}{2}}$.

questions.subtopic: RMS Speed, Pressure, KE, Internal Energy
questions.question_text:
Match Column-I and Column-II and choose the correct match from the given choices.

Column-I: (A) Root mean square speed of gas molecules, (B) Pressure exerted by ideal gas, (C) Average kinetic energy of a molecule, (D) Total internal energy of 1 mole of a diatomic gas
Column-II: (P) $\frac{1}{3}nm\bar{v}^2$, (Q) $\sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$, (R) $\frac{5}{2}RT$, (S) $\frac{3}{2}k_BT$
questions.solution_text: RMS speed $= \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$ → (Q). Pressure $= \frac{1}{3}nm\bar{v}^2$ → (P). Average KE of molecule $= \frac{3}{2}k_BT$ → (S). Total internal energy of 1 mole diatomic gas (f=5): $U = \frac{1}{2}nfRT = \frac{5}{2}RT$ → (R). Answer: (A)-(Q), (B)-(P), (C)-(S), (D)-(R).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A body is executing simple harmonic motion with frequency '$n$', the frequency of its potential energy is
questions.solution_text: Displacement $x = A\sin(\omega t + \phi)$ has frequency $n_1 = \frac{\omega}{2\pi}$. Potential energy $U = \frac{1}{2}kA^2\sin^2(\omega t + \phi)$, which has $\sin^2$ dependence. Since $\sin^2\theta = \frac{1-\cos 2\theta}{2}$, the PE oscillates with frequency $n_2 = \frac{2\omega}{2\pi} = 2n_1 = 2n$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A cup of coffee cools from 90°C to 80°C in $t$ minutes, when the room temperature is 20°C. The time taken by a similar cup of coffee to cool from 80°C to 60°C at a room temperature same at 20°C is
questions.solution_text: Newton's law of cooling (average form): $-K\left(\frac{T_1+T_2}{2}-T_s\right) = \frac{T_1-T_2}{\Delta t}$. Case 1: $-K(85-20) = \frac{10}{t}$, so $K = \frac{-2}{13t}$. Case 2: $-K(70-20) = \frac{20}{t_1}$, so $\frac{2}{13t}(50) = \frac{20}{t_1}$, giving $t_1 = \frac{13t}{5}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A capacitor of capacitance '$C$', is connected across an ac source of voltage $V$, given by $V = V_0\sin\omega t$. The displacement current between the plates of the capacitor, would then be given by
questions.solution_text: Displacement current $I_d = C\frac{dV}{dt} = C\frac{d}{dt}(V_0\sin\omega t) = CV_0\omega\cos\omega t = V_0\omega C\cos\omega t$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The half-life of a radioactive nuclide is 100 hours. The fraction of original activity that will remain after 150 hours would be
questions.solution_text: Activity $A = A_0 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/T_{1/2}} = A_0 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{150/100} = A_0 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{3/2} = \frac{A_0}{2\sqrt{2}}$. So fraction $= \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$.
