questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Magnetic Field Inside and Outside a Thick Cable
questions.question_text: A thick current carrying cable of radius '$R$' carries current '$I$' uniformly distributed across its cross-section. The variation of magnetic field $B(r)$ due to the cable with the distance '$r$' from the axis of the cable is represented by

options.text: Graph showing B increasing then staying constant
Graph showing B linearly increasing throughout
Graph showing B linearly increasing inside, then decreasing as hyperbola outside
Graph showing B decreasing then increasing

questions.solution_text: From Ampere's law: For $r < R$: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi R^2} \cdot r$, so $B \propto r$ (linear increase). For $r \geq R$: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$, so $B \propto \frac{1}{r}$ (hyperbolic decrease). The graph shows linear increase inside, then hyperbolic decrease outside.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question_text: An electromagnetic wave of wavelength '$\lambda$' is incident on a photosensitive surface of negligible work function. If '$m$' mass is of photoelectron emitted from the surface has de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda_d$, then
questions.solution_text: With negligible work function: $\frac{hc}{\lambda} = k = \frac{P^2}{2m}$, so $P = \sqrt{\frac{2mhc}{\lambda}}$. De-Broglie wavelength: $\lambda_d = \frac{h}{P} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mhc/\lambda}}$. So $\sqrt{\lambda} = \lambda_d \sqrt{\frac{2mc}{h}}$, hence $\lambda = \left(\frac{2mc}{h}\right)\lambda_d^2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The escape velocity from the Earth's surface is $v$. The escape velocity from the surface of another planet having a radius, four times that of Earth and same mass density is
questions.solution_text: Escape velocity $v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}} = \sqrt{\frac{8G\pi\rho R^2}{3}}$. For same density, $v_e \propto R$. New planet has $R_1 = 4R$, so $v_1 = 4v$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Dimensions of Energy in terms of F, A, T
questions.question_text: If force [F], acceleration [A] and time [T] are chosen as the fundamental physical quantities. Find the dimensions of energy.
questions.solution_text: Let $E \propto F^a A^b T^c$. $[ML^2T^{-2}] = [MLT^{-2}]^a [LT^{-2}]^b [T]^c = [M^a L^{a+b} T^{-2a-2b+c}]$. Comparing: $a=1$, $a+b=2 \Rightarrow b=1$, $-2-2+c=-2 \Rightarrow c=2$. So $[E] = [FAT^2]$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two conducting circular loops of radii $R_1$ and $R_2$ are placed in the same plane with their centres coinciding. If $R_1 >> R_2$, the mutual inductance $M$ between them will be directly proportional to
questions.solution_text: Magnetic field at centre of outer loop: $B = \frac{\mu_0 i}{2R_1}$. Flux through inner coil: $\phi = B \times \pi R_2^2 = \frac{\mu_0 i}{2R_1} \times \pi R_2^2$. Since $\phi = Mi$, we get $M = \frac{\mu_0 \pi}{2} \cdot \frac{R_2^2}{R_1}$. Hence $M \propto \frac{R_2^2}{R_1}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A point object is placed at a distance of 60 cm from a convex lens of focal length 30 cm. If a plane mirror were put perpendicular to the principal axis of the lens and at a distance of 40 cm from it, the final image would be formed at a distance of

options.text: 20 cm from the lens, it would be a real image
30 cm from the lens, it would be a real image
30 cm from the plane mirror, it would be a virtual image
20 cm from the plane mirror, it would be a virtual image

questions.solution_text: Using lens formula: $v_1 = 60$ cm (image by lens). Mirror is at 40 cm, so image acts as virtual object at 20 cm behind mirror. Mirror produces image 20 cm in front of it. For second refraction through lens: $u = -20$ cm, $f = 30$ cm, giving $v = -60$ cm. Final image is 60 - 40 = 20 cm from mirror, virtual.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Three resistors having resistances $r_1$, $r_2$ and $r_3$ are connected as shown in the given circuit. The ratio $\dfrac{i_3}{i_1}$ of currents in terms of resistances used in the circuit is
questions.solution_text: In parallel combination of $r_2$ and $r_3$: $i_2 r_2 = i_3 r_3$, so $i_2 = \frac{i_3 r_3}{r_2}$. By Kirchhoff's first law: $i_1 = i_2 + i_3 = i_3\left(\frac{r_3}{r_2} + 1\right) = i_3\frac{r_2+r_3}{r_2}$. Therefore $\frac{i_3}{i_1} = \frac{r_2}{r_2+r_3}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: For the given circuit, the input digital signals are applied at the terminals A, B and C. What would be the output at the terminal y?

options.text: Output y is always high (5V) throughout
Output y alternates with specific pattern

questions.solution_text: Output of combination: $y = A \cdot B + \overline{B \cdot C}$. From truth table analysis for all time intervals, $y$ is always 1 (5V). So output $y$ is always high.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit containing 5.0 H inductor, 80 $\mu$F capacitor and 40 $\Omega$ resistor is connected to 230 V variable frequency ac source. The angular frequencies of the source at which power transferred to the circuit is half the power at the resonant angular frequency are likely to be
questions.solution_text: Resonant frequency $\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5 \times 80 \times 10^{-6}}} = 50$ rad/s. Half-power frequencies: $\omega = \omega_0 \pm \frac{R}{2L} = 50 \pm \frac{40}{2 \times 5} = 50 \pm 4$. So $\omega_L = 46$ rad/s and $\omega_H = 54$ rad/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A car starts from rest and accelerates at 5 m/s². At $t = 4$ s, a ball is dropped out of a window by a person sitting in the car. What is the velocity and acceleration of the ball at $t = 6$ s? (Take $g = 10$ m/s²)
questions.solution_text: At $t=4$ s, car velocity $= 5 \times 4 = 20$ m/s. Ball is dropped with $v_x = 20$ m/s. After 2 s: $v_y = gt = 10 \times 2 = 20$ m/s. Magnitude $= \sqrt{20^2 + 20^2} = 20\sqrt{2}$ m/s. Acceleration is $g = 10$ m/s² (free fall).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Maximum Height for Projectile Below Escape Velocity
questions.question_text: A particle of mass '$m$' is projected with a velocity $v = kV_e$ ($k < 1$) from the surface of the earth. ($V_e$ = escape velocity). The maximum height above the surface reached by the particle is
questions.solution_text: Using energy conservation: $\frac{1}{2}mv^2 - \frac{GMm}{R} = -\frac{GMm}{R+h}$. With $v = kV_e$ and $V_e = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}}$: $k^2 = \frac{h}{R+h}$, giving $Rk^2 = h(1-k^2)$, so $h = \frac{Rk^2}{1-k^2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Angle of Projection for Given Height
questions.question_text: A particle moving in a circle of radius $R$ with a uniform speed takes a time $T$ to complete one revolution. If this particle were projected with the same speed at an angle '$\theta$' to the horizontal, the maximum height attained by it equals 4R. The angle of projection $\theta$ is then given by:
questions.solution_text: Speed $U = \frac{2\pi R}{T}$. Maximum height $H = \frac{U^2\sin^2\theta}{2g} = 4R$. So $\sin^2\theta = \frac{8gR}{U^2} = \frac{8gR}{4\pi^2R^2/T^2} = \frac{2gT^2}{\pi^2 R}$. Hence $\theta = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2gT^2}{\pi^2 R}\right)^{1/2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In the product $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}) = q\vec{v} \times (B\hat{i} + B\hat{j} + B_0\hat{k})$. For $q = 1$ and $\vec{v} = 2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}$ and $\vec{F} = 4\hat{i} - 20\hat{j} + 12\hat{k}$. What will be the complete expression for $\vec{B}$?
questions.solution_text: From $\vec{F} = \vec{v} \times \vec{B}$, solving the determinant gives $B = -6$, $B_0 = -8$. Hence $\vec{B} = -6\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} - 8\hat{k}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A ball of mass 0.15 kg is dropped from a height 10 m, strikes the ground and rebounds to the same height. The magnitude of impulse imparted to the ball is ($g = 10$ m/s²) nearly
questions.solution_text: Velocity at ground: $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 10} = 10\sqrt{2}$ m/s. Impulse $= \Delta p = m(v_f - v_i) = 0.15 \times (10\sqrt{2} - (-10\sqrt{2})) = 0.15 \times 20\sqrt{2} = 2 \times 0.15 \times 10\sqrt{2} = 4.2$ kg m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Magnetic Moment of Current Carrying Coil
questions.question_text: A uniform conducting wire of length $12a$ and resistance '$R$' is wound up as a current carrying coil in the shape of (i) an equilateral triangle of side '$a$' and (ii) a square of side '$a$'. The magnetic dipole moments of the coil in each case respectively are
questions.solution_text: Number of turns for triangle: $N_1 = 12a / 3a = 4$. Area of equilateral triangle $= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2$. $M_1 = N_1 I A = 4 \times I \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2 = \sqrt{3}\,Ia^2$. For square: $N_2 = 12a/4a = 3$. $M_2 = 3 \times I \times a^2 = 3\,Ia^2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Twenty seven drops of same size are charged at 200 V each. They combine to form a bigger drop. Calculate the potential of the bigger drop.
questions.solution_text: Volume conservation: $27 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3$, so $R = 3r$. Total charge $Q = 27q$. $V_{big} = \frac{kQ}{R} = \frac{k(27q)}{3r} = 9 \times \frac{kq}{r} = 9 \times 220 = 1980$ V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncert_chapter_name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question_text: A uniform rod of length 200 cm and mass 500 g is balanced on a wedge placed at 40 cm mark. A mass of 2 kg is suspended from the rod at 20 cm and another unknown mass '$m$' is suspended from the rod at 160 cm mark. Find the value of '$m$' such that the rod is in equilibrium. ($g = 10$ m/s²)
questions.solution_text: Taking torques about fulcrum (40 cm mark): Torque by 2 kg mass $= 2g \times 20 \times 10^{-2} = 4$ N·m (anticlockwise). Torque by rod's CM (at 100 cm) $= 0.5g \times 60 \times 10^{-2} = 3$ N·m (clockwise). Torque by $m$ $= mg \times 120 \times 10^{-2} = 12mg$ (clockwise). For equilibrium: $4 = 3 + 12mg$, giving $m = \frac{1}{12}$ kg.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Moment of Inertia of Partial Ring
questions.ncert_chapter_name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question_text: From a circular ring of mass '$M$' and radius '$R$' an arc corresponding to a 90° sector is removed. The moment of inertia of the remaining part of the ring about an axis passing through the centre of the ring and perpendicular to the plane of the ring is '$K$' times '$MR^2$'. Then the value of '$K$' is
questions.solution_text: Mass of remaining part $= \frac{3M}{4}$. MOI of remaining part $= \int dm \cdot r^2 = R^2 \int dm = R^2 \times \frac{3M}{4} = \frac{3MR^2}{4}$. So $K = \frac{3}{4}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A step down transformer connected to an ac mains supply of 220 V is made to operate at 11 V, 44 W lamp. Ignoring power losses in the transformer, what is the current in the primary circuit?
questions.solution_text: For ideal transformer: Input power = Output power. $V_P I_P = P_{output} = 44$ W. $I_P = \frac{44}{220} = 0.2$ A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.question_text: Dihedral angle of least stable conformer of ethane is:
questions.solution_text: Ethane has two conformers: (i) Eclipsed and (ii) Staggered. Eclipsed conformer is least stable while staggered is most stable. In eclipsed conformer the dihedral angle is 0°.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Noble gases are named because of their inertness towards reactivity. Identify an incorrect statement about them.

options.text: Noble gases are sparingly soluble in water
Noble gases have very high melting and boiling points
Noble gases have weak dispersion forces
Noble gases have large positive values of electron gain enthalpy

questions.solution_text: Noble gases have weak dispersion forces hence they have low melting and boiling points, not high. Option (2) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The major product of the following chemical reaction is: $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CH-CH=CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \xrightarrow{(C_6H_5CO)_2O_2}$?
questions.solution_text: Peroxide effect (anti-Markovnikov addition): Br· adds to the less substituted carbon. The more stable secondary free radical forms at C3, then H is abstracted from HBr. Major product is $(CH_3)_2CH-CH_2-CH_2Br$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A particular station of All India Radio, New Delhi broadcasts on a frequency of 1,368 kHz (kilohertz). The wavelength of the electromagnetic radiation emitted by the transmitter is: [speed of light $c = 3.0 \times 10^8$ ms$^{-1}$]
questions.solution_text: $\lambda = \frac{c}{\nu} = \frac{3 \times 10^8}{1368 \times 10^3} = \frac{3 \times 10^8}{1.368 \times 10^6} = 219.3$ m.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.ncert_chapter_name: The d and f Block Elements
questions.question_text: The incorrect statement among the following is:

options.text: Actinoid contraction is greater for element to element than lanthanoid contraction
Most of the trivalent Lanthanoid ions are colorless in the solid state
Lanthanoids are good conductors of heat and electricity
Actinoids are highly reactive metals, especially when finely divided.

questions.solution_text: Many trivalent lanthanoid ions are coloured both in the solid state and in aqueous solutions (not colorless). Hence option (2) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Right option for the number of tetrahedral and octahedral voids in hexagonal primitive unit cell are:
questions.solution_text: Each hexagonal unit cell contains 6 atoms. Number of tetrahedral voids = 2N = 12. Number of octahedral voids = N = 6.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Identify the compound that will react with Hinsberg's reagent to give a solid which dissolves in alkali.
questions.solution_text: Primary amine reacts with Hinsberg's reagent (C₆H₅SO₂Cl) to give N-substituted sulphonamide which dissolves in alkali (has N-H). Secondary amine gives product insoluble in alkali. Tertiary amine does not react.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following reactions is the metal displacement reaction? Choose the right option.
questions.solution_text: Reactions (1) and (4) are decomposition. Reactions (2) and (3) are displacement; (2) is metal displacement (Al displaces Cr from its oxide). Reaction (3) is non-metal (H) displacement.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Aspirin and Paracetamol belong to the class of narcotic analgesics.
Statement II: Morphine and Heroin are non-narcotic analgesics.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true

questions.solution_text: Aspirin and Paracetamol are non-narcotic analgesics. Morphine and Heroin are narcotic analgesics. Both statements are false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: What is the IUPAC name of the organic compound formed in the following chemical reaction? Acetone $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) } C_2H_5MgBr,\text{ dry ether}}_{\text{(ii) } H_2O, H^+}$ Product
questions.solution_text: Acetone (CH₃COCH₃) reacts with C₂H₅MgBr. The ethyl Grignard adds to the carbonyl to give 2-methylbutan-2-ol: $CH_3-C(OH)(C_2H_5)-CH_3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Statement I: Acid strength increases in the order given as HF << HCl << HBr << HI.
Statement II: As the size of the elements F, Cl, Br, I increases down the group, the bond strength of HF, HCl, HBr and HI decreases and so the acid strength increases.

options.text: Both statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true

questions.solution_text: As size of halogen increases down the group, H-X bond length increases, bond enthalpy decreases, and acidic strength increases. Order: HI > HBr > HCl > HF. Both statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Relationship Between Cp and Cv for Ideal Gas
questions.question_text: Which one among the following is the correct option for right relationship between $C_P$ and $C_V$ for one mole of ideal gas?
questions.solution_text: $\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta(PV) = \Delta U + R\Delta T$. So $C_P\Delta T = C_V\Delta T + R\Delta T$, giving $C_P - C_V = R$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) PCl₅, (b) SF₆, (c) BrF₅, (d) BF₃
List-II: (i) Square pyramidal, (ii) Trigonal planar, (iii) Octahedral, (iv) Trigonal bipyramidal
questions.solution_text: PCl₅: sp³d, trigonal bipyramidal (iv). SF₆: sp³d², octahedral (iii). BrF₅: sp³d², square pyramidal (i). BF₃: sp², trigonal planar (ii).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The following solutions were prepared by dissolving 10 g of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) in 250 ml of water (P₁), 10 g of urea (CH₄N₂O) in 250 ml of water (P₂) and 10 g of sucrose (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) in 250 ml of water (P₃). The right option for the decreasing order of osmotic pressure is:
questions.solution_text: Osmotic pressure $\pi = iCRT$. With equal mass in equal volume: higher molar mass → lower concentration → lower osmotic pressure. Molar masses: Urea (60) < Glucose (180) < Sucrose (342). So $P_2 > P_1 > P_3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.ncert_chapter_name: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.question_text: Which one of the following methods can be used to obtain highly pure metal which is liquid at room temperature?
questions.solution_text: Distillation method is used for purification of metals having low boiling point such as Hg, Zn etc. Mercury is liquid at room temperature and is purified by distillation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Tritium, a radioactive isotope of hydrogen, emits which of the following particles?
questions.solution_text: Tritium ($^3_1H$ or T) is the only radioactive isotope of hydrogen. It emits low energy $\beta^-$ particles (half-life = 12.33 years).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The correct option for the number of body centred unit cells in all 14 types of Bravais lattice unit cells is:
questions.solution_text: Body centred unit cell is present in cubic, tetragonal and orthorhombic crystal systems — 3 crystal systems total.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The major product formed in dehydrohalogenation reaction of 2-Bromo pentane is Pent-2-ene. This product formation is based on?
questions.solution_text: Saytzeff's rule states that in dehydrohalogenation, the preferred product is the more substituted alkene (having more alkyl groups on doubly bonded carbons). Pent-2-ene is more substituted than pent-1-ene, hence it is the major product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.ncert_chapter_name: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.question_text: The maximum temperature that can be achieved in blast furnace is:
questions.solution_text: Maximum temperature achievable in blast furnace is upto 2200 K (NCERT states 2170 K in figure).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The molar conductance of NaCl, HCl and CH₃COONa at infinite dilution are 126.45, 426.16 and 91.0 S cm² mol⁻¹ respectively. The molar conductance of CH₃COOH at infinite dilution is:
questions.solution_text: $\Lambda^\circ_m(CH_3COOH) = \Lambda^\circ_m(CH_3COONa) + \Lambda^\circ_m(HCl) - \Lambda^\circ_m(NaCl) = 91.0 + 426.16 - 126.45 = 390.71$ S cm² mol⁻¹.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Ethylene diaminetetraacetate (EDTA) ion is:

options.text: Hexadentate ligand with four 'O' and two 'N' donor atoms
Bidentate ligand with two 'N' donor atoms
Tridentate ligand with three 'N' donor atoms

questions.solution_text: EDTA is a hexadentate ligand having four donor oxygen atoms (from carboxylate groups) and two donor nitrogen atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The structures of beryllium chloride in solid state and vapour phase, are:
questions.solution_text: BeCl₂ has chain structure in solid state (due to bridging Cl). In vapour phase it tends to form a chloro-bridged dimer (Be₂Cl₄).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.question_text: The correct structure of 2,6-Dimethyl-dec-4-ene is

options.text: Structure with methyl at C2 and C6, double bond at C4
Structure with methyl at C2 and C6, double bond at C5
Structure with methyl at C3 and C6
Structure with methyl at C2 and C7

questions.solution_text: 2,6-Dimethyl-dec-4-ene: 10-carbon chain (dec), double bond between C4 and C5 (ene), methyl groups at C2 and C6.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The right option for the statement 'Tyndall effect is exhibited by', is:
questions.solution_text: Tyndall effect is exhibited by colloidal solutions only. NaCl, glucose, and urea solutions are true solutions. Starch solution is a colloidal solution and shows Tyndall effect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which one of the following polymers is prepared by addition polymerisation?
questions.solution_text: Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene) is prepared by addition polymerisation of tetrafluoroethene. Dacron, Nylon-66 and Novolac are condensation polymers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The RBC deficiency is deficiency disease of:
questions.solution_text: Deficiency of vitamin B₁₂ causes Pernicious anaemia, which is RBC deficiency in haemoglobin.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The correct sequence of bond enthalpy of 'C—X' bond is:
questions.solution_text: As size of halogen increases F→I, bond length increases, bond enthalpy decreases. So CH₃-F (452) > CH₃-Cl (351) > CH₃-Br (293) > CH₃-I (234) kJ/mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.question_text: An organic compound contains 78% (by wt.) carbon and remaining percentage of hydrogen. The right option for the empirical formula of this compound is: [Atomic wt. of C is 12, H is 1]
questions.solution_text: C: 78/12 = 6.5 moles; H: 22/1 = 22 moles. Ratio C:H = 6.5:22 = 1:3.38 ≈ 1:3. Empirical formula: CH₃.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Covalent Character of Alkaline Earth Metal Halides
questions.question_text: Among the following alkaline earth metal halides, one which is covalent and soluble in organic solvents is:
questions.solution_text: Due to small size and high charge density of Be²⁺, BeCl₂ is essentially covalent and soluble in organic solvents. All other alkaline earth metal chlorides are ionic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: BF₃ is planar and electron deficient compound. Hybridization and number of electrons around the central atom, respectively are:
questions.solution_text: BF₃: B has 3 bond pairs, no lone pairs. Hybridisation = sp². Number of electrons around B = 3 × 2 = 6. Shape is trigonal planar.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: pH of Salt of Weak Acid and Weak Base
questions.question_text: The pKb of dimethylamine and pKa of acetic acid are 3.27 and 4.77 respectively at T (K). The correct option for the pH of dimethylammonium acetate solution is:
questions.solution_text: For salt of weak acid and weak base: $pH = 7 + \frac{1}{2}(pK_a - pK_b) = 7 + \frac{1}{2}(4.77 - 3.27) = 7 + 0.75 = 7.75$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Choose the correct option for graphical representation of Boyle's law, which shows a graph of pressure vs. volume of a gas at different temperatures:
questions.solution_text: By Boyle's law $PV = k$ (constant at fixed T). P vs V graph is rectangular hyperbola. PV increases with temperature, so higher temperature curve lies further from origin (600K outermost).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Potential Energy Profile for Exothermic Reaction
questions.question_text: For a reaction A → B, enthalpy of reaction is −4.2 kJ mol⁻¹ and enthalpy of activation is 9.6 kJ mol⁻¹. The correct potential energy profile for the reaction is shown in option:

options.text: B higher than A with large hump
B lower than A, activation energy from A side greater
A and B at same level

questions.solution_text: Reaction is exothermic (ΔH = -4.2 kJ/mol) so B is lower than A. $(E_a)_b = (E_a)_f - \Delta H_{rxn} = 9.6 - (-4.2) = 13.8$ kJ/mol. $(E_a)_f < (E_a)_b$. Correct graph shows B lower than A with forward activation energy smaller than reverse.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.question_text: The compound which shows metamerism is:
questions.solution_text: C₄H₁₀O can be ethers which exhibit metamerism: CH₃-CH₂-O-CH₂-CH₃ and CH₃-O-CH(CH₃)-CH₃ and CH₃-O-CH₂-CH₂-CH₃ are metamers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.ncert_chapter_name: The d and f Block Elements
questions.question_text: Zr (Z = 40) and Hf (Z = 72) have similar atomic and ionic radii because of:
questions.solution_text: Lanthanoid contraction causes the radii of third transition series members to be very similar to corresponding second series members. Zr (160 pm) ≈ Hf (159 pm) due to lanthanoid contraction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻, (b) [Fe(H₂O)₆]³⁺, (c) [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻, (d) [Fe(H₂O)₆]²⁺
List-II: (i) 5.92 BM, (ii) 0 BM, (iii) 4.90 BM, (iv) 1.73 BM
questions.solution_text: [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻: Fe³⁺ with strong field CN⁻, 1 unpaired e⁻, μ = 1.73 BM (iv). [Fe(H₂O)₆]³⁺: Fe³⁺ with weak field, 5 unpaired e⁻, μ = 5.92 BM (i). [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻: Fe²⁺ with CN⁻, 0 unpaired e⁻, μ = 0 BM (ii). [Fe(H₂O)₆]²⁺: Fe²⁺ with H₂O, 4 unpaired e⁻, μ = 4.90 BM (iii).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The reagent 'R' in the given sequence of chemical reaction is: (Conversion of diazonium salt to arene using reagent R)
questions.solution_text: Diazonium salt reacts with ethanol (C₂H₅OH) to give arene (replacement of diazonium group by H). Reagent R is C₂H₅OH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: From the following pairs of ions which one is not an iso-electronic pair?
questions.solution_text: Fe²⁺ has 24 electrons; Mn²⁺ has 23 electrons. They are not isoelectronic. Mn²⁺ and Fe³⁺ both have 23 electrons (isoelectronic).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The slope of Arrhenius plot $\left(\ln k \text{ v/s } \dfrac{1}{T}\right)$ of first order reaction is $-5 \times 10^3$ K. The value of $E_a$ of the reaction is: [Given R = 8.314 JK⁻¹mol⁻¹]
questions.solution_text: Slope $= -\frac{E_a}{R}$. So $E_a = -\text{slope} \times R = 5 \times 10^3 \times 8.314 = 41570$ J/mol $= 41.5$ kJ/mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For irreversible expansion of an ideal gas under isothermal condition, the correct option is:
questions.solution_text: Isothermal process: $\Delta T = 0$, so $\Delta U = nC_V\Delta T = 0$. Irreversible process is spontaneous, so $\Delta S_{total} > 0$ (not zero).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In which one of the following arrangements the given sequence is not strictly according to the properties indicated against it?

options.text: HF < HCl < HBr < HI : Increasing acidic strength
H₂O < H₂S < H₂Se < H₂Te : Increasing pKₐ values
NH₃ < PH₃ < AsH₃ < SbH₃ : Increasing acidic character
CO₂ < SiO₂ < SnO₂ < PbO₂ : Increasing oxidizing power

questions.solution_text: Stronger acid has lower pKₐ. Going down group 16, acidity increases (H₂O < H₂S < H₂Se < H₂Te), so pKₐ decreases (not increases). The correct order of pKₐ: H₂O > H₂S > H₂Se > H₂Te. Option (2) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The intermediate compound 'X' in the following chemical reaction is: $\text{Toluene} + CrO_2Cl_2 \xrightarrow{CS_2} X \xrightarrow{H_3O^+}$ Benzaldehyde
questions.solution_text: Etard's reaction: Toluene reacts with CrO₂Cl₂ in CS₂ to form chromium complex $C_6H_5-CH(OCrOHCl_2)_2$ as intermediate X. Hydrolysis with H₃O⁺ gives benzaldehyde.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The correct option for the value of vapour pressure of a solution at 45°C with benzene to octane in molar ratio 3:2 is: [At 45°C vapour pressure of benzene is 280 mm Hg and that of octane is 420 mm Hg. Assume Ideal gas]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The molar conductivity of 0.007 M acetic acid is 20 S cm² mol⁻¹. What is the dissociation constant of acetic acid? [$\Lambda^\circ_{H^+} = 350$, $\Lambda^\circ_{CH_3COO^-} = 50$ S cm² mol⁻¹]
questions.solution_text: $\Lambda^\circ_m = 400$ S cm² mol⁻¹. $\alpha = \Lambda_m / \Lambda^\circ_m = 20/400 = 1/20$. $K_a = \frac{C\alpha^2}{1-\alpha} \approx C\alpha^2 = 7 \times 10^{-3} \times (1/20)^2 = 1.75 \times 10^{-5}$ mol L⁻¹.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: $CH_3CH_2COO^-Na^+ \xrightarrow{NaOH, +?}_{\text{Heat}} CH_3CH_3 + Na_2CO_3$. Consider the above reaction and identify the missing reagent/chemical.
questions.solution_text: Alkane is produced by heating sodium salt of carboxylic acid with sodalime (NaOH + CaO in 3:1 ratio). CaO is the missing reagent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
(a) Benzene + CO, HCl/AlCl₃ → (b) R-CO-CH₃ + NaOX → (c) R-CH₂-OH + R'COOH → (d) R-CH₂COOH + X₂/Red P then H₂O →
List-II: (i) Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky, (ii) Gattermann-Koch, (iii) Haloform, (iv) Esterification
questions.solution_text: (a) Gattermann-Koch (ii); (b) Haloform reaction (iii); (c) Esterification (iv); (d) Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (i).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The product formed in the following chemical reaction is: Keto ester compound $\xrightarrow{NaBH_4, C_2H_5OH}$?

options.text: Hydroxy ester (both ketone and ester reduced)
Hydroxy ester (only ketone reduced, ester intact)

questions.solution_text: NaBH₄ is a mild reducing agent. It reduces carbonyl groups (ketones, aldehydes) to alcohols but does NOT reduce esters. Only the ketone is reduced; the ester group remains intact.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following molecules is non-polar in nature?
questions.solution_text: SbCl₅ has trigonal bipyramidal geometry; net vector sum of bond moments = zero, so it is non-polar. POCl₃, CH₂O, and NO₂ are polar molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
(a) 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃, (b) HOCl → OH• + Cl•, (c) CaCO₃ + H₂SO₄ → CaSO₄ + H₂O + CO₂, (d) NO₂ → NO + O
List-II: (i) Acid rain, (ii) Smog, (iii) Ozone depletion, (iv) Tropospheric pollution
questions.solution_text: (a) SO₂→SO₃ = tropospheric pollution (iv). (b) HOCl photolysis gives Cl• = ozone depletion (iii). (c) CaCO₃ + H₂SO₄ = acid rain effect (i). (d) NO₂ photolysis = smog (ii).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Choose the correct option for the total pressure (in atm.) in a mixture of 4 g O₂ and 2 g H₂ confined in a total volume of one litre at 0°C: [Given R = 0.082 L atm mol⁻¹K⁻¹, T = 273 K]

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following plants is monoecious?
questions.solution_text: When male and female sex organs are present on same plant body, such plants are said to be monoecious. Most of the species of Chara are monoecious. Cycas circinalis, Carica papaya and Marchantia polymorpha are dioecious.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A typical angiosperm embryo sac at maturity is:
questions.solution_text: A typical angiospermic embryo sac has seven cells: three antipodals, one central cell, one egg cell and two synergids. The central cell has two polar nuclei, hence the embryo sac is eight nucleated.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Gemmae are present in
questions.solution_text: Gemmae are green, multicellular asexual buds produced by some liverworts like Marchantia. Mosses reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation and budding of protonema. Pteridophytes and Gymnosperms normally do not reproduce asexually.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: When the centromere is situated in the middle of two equal arms of chromosomes, the chromosome is referred as:
questions.solution_text: When the centromere is situated in the middle of two equal arms, the chromosome is Metacentric. Sub-metacentric: centromere slightly away from middle. Acrocentric: centromere very close to one end. Telocentric: centromere at terminal position.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following stages of meiosis involves division of centromere?
questions.solution_text: Division of centromere occurs in Anaphase II. Chromosomes form two parallel plates in metaphase I and one plate in metaphase II. Telophase II is the last stage where chromatids reach poles and start uncoiling.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: First Stable Product in C4 Plants
questions.question_text: The first stable product of CO2 fixation in Sorghum is
questions.solution_text: Sorghum is a C4 plant. The first stable product of CO2 fixation in Sorghum is oxaloacetic acid (OAA). The first stable product in C3 cycle is 3-phosphoglyceric acid. Pyruvic acid is the end product of glycolysis. Succinic acid is an intermediate in Krebs cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The factor that leads to Founder effect in a population is:
questions.solution_text: Change in gene frequency in a small population by chance is genetic drift. Genetic drift has two effects: bottle neck effect and founder's effect. When a few individuals are accidentally dispersed and act as founders of a new isolated population, founder's effect is observed.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is an incorrect statement?

options.text: Mature sieve tube elements possess a conspicuous nucleus and usual cytoplasmic organelles
Microbodies are present both in plant and animal cells
The perinuclear space forms a barrier between the materials present inside the nucleus and that of the cytoplasm
Nuclear pores act as passages for proteins and RNA molecules in both directions between nucleus and cytoplasm

questions.solution_text: A mature sieve tube element possesses a peripheral cytoplasm and a large central vacuole but lacks a nucleus. Hence option (1) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Amensalism can be represented as:
questions.solution_text: Amensalism is an interaction where one species inhibits the growth of another by secreting chemicals, while the first species is neither benefitted nor harmed. (+):(0) = commensalism; (+):(+) = mutualism; (–):(–) = competition.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The amount of nutrients, such as carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and calcium present in the soil at any given time, is referred as:
questions.solution_text: Amount of all inorganic substances or nutrients such as carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and calcium present in soil at any given time is referred as standing state. Standing crop refers to living material at different trophic levels at a given time.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following algae contains mannitol as reserve food material?
questions.solution_text: Ectocarpus is a brown alga (Phaeophyceae). Members of this class have mannitol and laminarin as stored food. Ulothrix and Volvox belong to Chlorophyceae (starch). Gracilaria is a red alga (Rhodophyceae) with floridean starch.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Inspite of interspecific competition in nature, which mechanism the competing species might have evolved for their survival?
questions.solution_text: Inspite of interspecific competition, competing species may co-exist by resource partitioning — dividing available resources so they use different portions, reducing direct competition.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spores. Such plants are known as:
questions.solution_text: Plants like Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spores: microspores and macrospores. They are known as heterosporous. Most pteridophytes produce a single type of spore and are called homosporous.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The site of perception of light in plants during photoperiodism is
questions.solution_text: The site of perception of light in plants during photoperiodism is leaf. The site of perception of low temperature stimulus during vernalisation is shoot apex and embryo.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Plants follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called
questions.solution_text: Plants show plasticity — the ability to follow different pathways and produce different structures in response to environment.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Cristae, (b) Thylakoids, (c) Centromere, (d) Cisternae — (i) Primary constriction in chromosome, (ii) Disc-shaped sacs in Golgi apparatus, (iii) Infoldings in mitochondria, (iv) Flattened membranous sacs in stroma of plastids
questions.solution_text: Cristae: infoldings in mitochondria (iii). Thylakoids: flattened membranous sacs in stroma of plastids (iv). Centromere: primary constriction in chromosome (i). Cisternae: disc-shaped sacs in Golgi apparatus (ii).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Cohesion, (b) Adhesion, (c) Surface tension, (d) Guttation — (i) More attraction in liquid phase, (ii) Mutual attraction among water molecules, (iii) Water loss in liquid phase, (iv) Attraction towards polar surfaces
questions.solution_text: Cohesion = mutual attraction among water molecules (ii). Adhesion = attraction towards polar surfaces (iv). Surface tension = more attraction in liquid phase (i). Guttation = water loss in liquid phase from leaf margins (iii).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: DNA strands on a gel stained with ethidium bromide when viewed under UV radiation, appear as
questions.solution_text: After the bands are stained with ethidium bromide (an intercalating agent that stacks between nitrogenous bases), they are viewed in UV light and appear bright orange in colour.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The term used for transfer of pollen grains from anthers of one plant to stigma of a different plant which, during pollination, brings genetically different types of pollen grains to stigma, is:
questions.solution_text: Xenogamy: transfer of pollen from one plant to stigma of a different plant (genetically different). Geitonogamy: transfer within same plant. Cleistogamy: flower does not open. Chasmogamy: flowers remain open.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following algae produce Carrageen?
questions.solution_text: The cell wall of red algae is composed of agar, carrageen and funori along with cellulose. Brown algae cell wall contains algin. Green algae cell wall is composed of cellulose and pectin. Blue-green algae cell wall is composed of mucopeptides.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.text: Pyramid of biomass in sea is generally inverted.
Pyramid of biomass in sea is generally upright.
Pyramid of energy is always upright.
Pyramid of numbers in a grassland ecosystem is upright.

questions.solution_text: Pyramid of biomass in sea is inverted — biomass of zooplanktons is higher than that of phytoplanktons as the latter multiply much faster though having shorter life span. Pyramid of energy is always upright.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the equation GPP – R = NPP, R represents:
questions.solution_text: In GPP – R = NPP, R refers to respiratory loss. GPP is gross primary productivity and NPP is net primary productivity.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Diadelphous stamens are found in
questions.solution_text: Stamens are diadelphous when united in two bundles e.g. Pea. China rose has monoadelphous stamens. Citrus has polyadelphous stamens.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: When gene targetting involving gene amplification is attempted in an individual's tissue to treat disease, it is known as:
questions.solution_text: Gene therapy is a collection of methods that allows correction of a gene defect diagnosed in a child/embryo. Biopiracy is the use of bio-resources without proper authorisation. Molecular diagnosis determines the nature and cause of a disease.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Lenticels, (b) Phellogen, (c) Secondary cortex, (d) Cork — (i) Phellogen, (ii) Suberin deposition, (iii) Exchange of gases, (iv) Phelloderm
questions.solution_text: Lenticels: exchange of gases (iii). Phellogen: cork cambium (i). Secondary cortex (Phelloderm): (iv). Cork: suberin deposition in cell walls (ii).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The production of gametes by the parents, formation of zygotes, the F1 and F2 plants, can be understood from a diagram called:
questions.solution_text: The production of gametes (n) by the parents (2n), the formation of the zygote (2n), the F1 and F2 plants can be understood from a diagram called Punnett square.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a correct sequence of steps in a PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction)?
questions.solution_text: PCR steps: (1) Denaturation (~94°C): dsDNA strands separate. (2) Annealing: primers anneal to 3' end of template DNA. (3) Extension: Taq polymerase adds nucleotides to 3'OH end of primers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.question_text: Mutations in plant cells can be induced by:
questions.solution_text: Gamma rays, X-rays and UV-rays are physical mutagens that cause mutation. Kinetin and zeatin are cytokinins. Infrared rays cause only a heating effect.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Protoplast fusion, (b) Plant tissue culture, (c) Meristem culture, (d) Micropropagation — (i) Totipotency, (ii) Pomato, (iii) Somaclones, (iv) Virus free plants
questions.solution_text: Protoplast fusion → Pomato (ii). Plant tissue culture → Totipotency (i). Meristem culture → Virus free plants (iv). Micropropagation → Somaclones (iii).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: During the purification process for recombinant DNA technology, addition of chilled ethanol precipitates out:
questions.solution_text: Enzymes like protease and RNase break down proteins and RNA. Once all these are broken down, DNA is left which is precipitated out by adding chilled ethanol.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Complete the flow chart on central dogma: DNA $\xrightarrow{(b)}$ mRNA $\xrightarrow{(c)}$ (d), where (a) is a process on DNA itself.
questions.solution_text: DNA → DNA = Replication (a). DNA → mRNA = Transcription (b). mRNA → Protein = Translation (c). The final product is Protein (d). Transduction is transfer of genetic material by bacteriophage.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an application of PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction)?
questions.solution_text: PCR is used for gene amplification, molecular diagnosis, and detection of mutations. Protein is not the target of PCR, so it plays no role in protein purification.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The plant hormone used to destroy weeds in a field
questions.solution_text: 2,4-D (a synthetic auxin) is widely used to remove broad-leaved weeds (dicotyledonous) in cereal crops (monocotyledonous plants). IAA and IBA are natural auxins; NAA is a synthetic auxin but not used as a weedicide.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Cells with active cell division capacity, (b) Tissue having all cells similar in structure and function, (c) Tissue having different types of cells, (d) Dead cells with highly thickened walls and narrow lumen — (i) Vascular tissues, (ii) Meristematic tissue, (iii) Sclereids, (iv) Simple tissue
questions.solution_text: Meristematic tissue: active cell division (ii). Simple tissue: all cells similar (iv). Vascular tissues: complex, different cell types (i). Sclereids: dead cells with thickened walls and narrow lumen (iii).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following are not secondary metabolites in plants?
questions.solution_text: Amino acids and glucose are primary metabolites with identifiable functions in normal physiological processes. Rubber, gums, morphine, codeine, vinblastin and curcumin are secondary metabolites whose roles in host organisms are not yet fully known.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.text: During aerobic respiration, role of oxygen is limited to the terminal stage
In ETC (Electron Transport Chain), one molecule of NADH + H+ gives rise to 2 ATP molecules, and one FADH2 gives rise to 3 ATP molecules
ATP is synthesized through complex V
Oxidation-reduction reactions produce proton gradient in respiration

questions.solution_text: In ETC, one NADH + H+ produces 3 ATP while one FADH2 produces 2 ATP. Option (2) reverses these values, making it incorrect. ATP is synthesised via complex V. Oxygen acts as terminal electron acceptor in ETS.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Match Column-I with Column-II: (a) Nitrococcus, (b) Rhizobium, (c) Thiobacillus, (d) Nitrobacter — (i) Denitrification, (ii) Conversion of ammonia to nitrite, (iii) Conversion of nitrite to nitrate, (iv) Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen to ammonia
questions.solution_text: Rhizobium: N2 fixation → NH3 (iv). Nitrococcus: NH3 → NO2- (ii). Nitrobacter: NO2- → NO3- (iii). Thiobacillus: denitrification NO2-/NO3- → N2 (i).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Match Column-I with Column-II: (a) %K(5)C1+2+(2)A(9)+1G1, (b) K(5)C(5)A5G(2), (c) P(3+3)A3+3G(3), (d) K2+2C4A2+4G(2) — (i) Brassicaceae, (ii) Liliaceae, (iii) Fabaceae, (iv) Solanaceae
questions.solution_text: Fabaceae: %K(5)C1+2+(2)A(9)+1G1 (iii). Solanaceae: K(5)C(5)A5G(2) (iv). Liliaceae: P(3+3)A3+3G(3) (ii). Brassicaceae: K2+2C4A2+4G(2) (i).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Identify the correct statement.

options.text: In capping, methyl guanosine triphosphate is added to the 3' end of hnRNA
RNA polymerase binds with Rho factor to terminate the process of transcription in bacteria
The coding strand in a transcription unit is copied to an mRNA
Split gene arrangement is characteristic of prokaryotes

questions.solution_text: RNA polymerase associates with Rho (ρ) factor to terminate transcription in bacteria — this is correct. Capping adds 5-methyl guanosine triphosphate at the 5' end (not 3'). The template (non-coding) strand is copied, not the coding strand. Split genes are characteristic of eukaryotes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Fusion of two cells is called Karyogamy
Fusion of protoplasms between two motile or non-motile gametes is called plasmogamy
Organisms that depend on living plants are called saprophytes
Some of the organisms can fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialized cells called sheath cells

questions.solution_text: Fusion of protoplasts of two cells is called plasmogamy — correct. Fusion of two nuclei is Karyogamy. Organisms depending on living plants are parasites; saprophytes grow on dead material. Nitrogen fixation in blue-green algae occurs in heterocysts, not sheath cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Select the correct pair.

options.text: Large colorless empty cells in the epidermis of grass leaves — Subsidiary cells
In dicot leaves, vascular bundles are surrounded by large thick-walled cells — Conjunctive tissue
Cells of medullary rays that form part of cambial ring — Interfascicular cambium
Loose parenchyma cells rupturing the epidermis and forming a lens shaped opening in bark — Spongy parenchyma

questions.solution_text: Medullary ray cells differentiate to give rise to interfascicular cambium — correct. Large colourless empty cells in grass epidermis = bulliform cells. Vascular bundles in dicot leaves surrounded by thick-walled cells = bundle sheath cells. Lens-shaped openings in bark = complementary cells (in lenticels).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: DNA fingerprinting involves identifying differences in some specific regions in DNA sequence, called as
questions.solution_text: DNA fingerprinting involves identifying differences in specific regions called repetitive DNA. The basis is VNTR (Variable Number of Tandem Repeats), a satellite DNA probe showing very high degree of polymorphism.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Pollen Grain Viability in Different Families
questions.question_text: In some members of which of the following pairs of families, pollen grains retain their viability for months after release?
questions.solution_text: In Solanaceae, Rosaceae and Leguminosae, pollen grains retain viability for several months. In cereals (Poaceae), pollen grains retain viability for only about 30 minutes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.text: Both ATP and NADPH + H+ are synthesized during non-cyclic photophosphorylation
Stroma lamellae have PS I only and lack NADP reductase
Grana lamellae have both PS I and PS II
Cyclic photophosphorylation involves both PS I and PS II

questions.solution_text: Cyclic photophosphorylation involves only PS I — option (4) is incorrect. Non-cyclic photophosphorylation involves both PS I and PS II and produces both ATP and NADPH. Grana lamellae have both PS I and PS II; stroma lamellae have only PS I and lack NADP reductase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: What is the role of RNA polymerase III in the process of transcription in eukaryotes?
questions.solution_text: RNA polymerase III transcribes tRNA, ScRNA, 5S rRNA and SnRNA. RNA polymerase I transcribes 5.8S, 18S and 28S rRNA. RNA polymerase II transcribes hnRNA (precursor of mRNA).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the exponential growth equation $N_t = N_0 e^{rt}$, e represents
questions.solution_text: In $N_t = N_0 e^{rt}$, e represents the base of natural logarithms. Nt = population density after time t; N0 = population density at time zero; r = intrinsic rate of natural increase (biotic potential).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Now a days it is possible to detect the mutated gene causing cancer by allowing radioactive probe to hybridise its complimentary DNA in a clone of cells, followed by its detection using autoradiography because:

options.text: mutated gene partially appears on a photographic film
mutated gene completely and clearly appears on a photographic film
mutated gene does not appear on a photographic film as the probe has no complementarity with it
mutated gene does not appear on photographic film as the probe has complementarity with it

questions.solution_text: The mutated gene will not appear on the photographic film because the probe does not have complementarity with the mutated gene. The probe hybridises only with the normal/complementary sequence.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Protein, (b) Unsaturated fatty acid, (c) Nucleic acid, (d) Polysaccharide — (i) C=C double bonds, (ii) Phosphodiester bonds, (iii) Glycosidic bonds, (iv) Peptide bonds
questions.solution_text: Protein: amino acids linked by peptide bonds (iv). Unsaturated fatty acid: has C=C double bonds (i). Nucleic acid: nucleotides linked by phosphodiester bonds (ii). Polysaccharide: monosaccharides linked by glycosidic bonds (iii).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) S phase, (b) G2 phase, (c) Quiescent stage, (d) G1 phase — (i) Proteins are synthesized, (ii) Inactive phase, (iii) Interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication, (iv) DNA replication
questions.solution_text: S phase: DNA replication (iv). G2 phase: synthesis of proteins, RNA etc. (i). Quiescent stage: inactive stage (ii). G1 phase: interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication (iii).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Plasmid pBR322 has PstI restriction enzyme site within gene ampR that confers ampicillin resistance. If this enzyme is used for inserting a gene for β-galactoside production and the recombinant plasmid is inserted in an E.coli strain

options.text: It will not be able to confer ampicillin resistance to the host cell
The transformed cells will have the ability to resist ampicillin as well as produce β-galactoside
It will lead to lysis of host cell
It will be able to produce a novel protein with dual ability

questions.solution_text: When the gene for β-galactoside is inserted in the ampicillin resistance gene using PstI, the recombinant E. coli loses ampicillin resistance due to insertional inactivation of the antibiotic resistance gene.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Identify the incorrect pair
questions.solution_text: Ricin is a toxin obtained from Ricinus plant, not a drug. Vinblastin and curcumin are drugs. Morphine and codeine are alkaloids. Abrin is a toxin from plant Abrus. Concanavalin A is a lectin.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The fruit fly has 8 chromosomes (2n) in each cell. During interphase of Mitosis if the number of chromosomes at G1 phase is 8, what would be the number of chromosomes after S phase?
questions.solution_text: In S phase there is duplication of DNA but not chromosome number. So if the number of chromosomes at G1 phase is 8, the number remains 8 after S phase (though DNA content doubles).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Metamerism, (b) Canal system, (c) Comb plates, (d) Cnidoblasts — (i) Coelenterata, (ii) Ctenophora, (iii) Annelida, (iv) Porifera
questions.solution_text: Metamerism: Annelida (iii). Canal system: Porifera (iv). Comb plates: Ctenophora (ii) — help in locomotion. Cnidoblasts: Coelenterata/Cnidaria (i).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Vaults, (b) IUDs, (c) Vasectomy, (d) Tubectomy — (i) Entry of sperm through Cervix is blocked, (ii) Removal of Vas deferens, (iii) Phagocytosis of sperms within the Uterus, (iv) Removal of fallopian tube
questions.solution_text: Vaults: barrier method blocking sperm entry through cervix (i). IUDs: increase phagocytosis of sperms within uterus (iii). Vasectomy: removal/tying of vas deferens (ii). Tubectomy: removal of fallopian tube (iv).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: If Adenine makes 30% of the DNA molecule, what will be the percentage of Thymine, Guanine and Cytosine in it?
questions.solution_text: By Chargaff's rule: A = T and C = G. A = 30%, so T = 30%. Remaining = 100 − 60 = 40%, so G = C = 20% each.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following RNAs is not required for the synthesis of protein?
questions.solution_text: siRNA (small interfering RNA) is a class of double-stranded non-coding RNA involved in RNA interference, not in protein synthesis. mRNA carries genetic information, tRNA carries amino acids, rRNA forms ribosomes — all required for translation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an example of Hormone releasing IUD?
questions.solution_text: LNG-20 is a hormone releasing IUD which makes the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms. Multiload 375, CuT and Cu7 are copper releasing IUDs which suppress sperm motility and fertilizing capacity.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Succus entericus is referred to as:
questions.solution_text: Succus entericus is referred to as intestinal juice. Chyme is the acidic food present in the stomach. Pancreatic juice is the exocrine secretion of pancreatic acini. Gastric juice is secreted by gastric glands in the stomach.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Chronic auto immune disorder affecting neuro muscular junction leading to fatigue, weakening and paralysis of skeletal muscle is called as:
questions.solution_text: Myasthenia gravis is a chronic auto immune disorder affecting neuromuscular junction leading to fatigue, weakening and paralysis of skeletal muscle. Gout: uric acid crystal deposition in joints. Arthritis: inflammation of joints. Muscular dystrophy: genetic disorder with progressive skeletal muscle degeneration.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: With regard to insulin choose correct options. (a) C-peptide is not present in mature insulin. (b) The insulin produced by rDNA technology has C-peptide. (c) The pro-insulin has C-peptide. (d) A-peptide and B-peptide of insulin are interconnected by disulphide bridges.
questions.solution_text: Insulin is synthesized as a pro-hormone containing A-chain, B-chain and C-peptide. C-peptide is NOT present in mature insulin (humulin). Chains A and B are connected by interchain disulphide bridges. Insulin produced by rDNA technology does not have C-peptide (it is removed during processing).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which one of the following belongs to the family Muscidae?
questions.solution_text: Housefly belongs to family Muscidae, class Insecta, phylum Arthropoda. Fire flies: family Lampyridae. Grasshopper: family Acrididae. Cockroach: family Blattidae.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which is the 'Only enzyme' that has 'Capability' to catalyse Initiation, Elongation and Termination in the process of transcription in prokaryotes?
questions.solution_text: In prokaryotes, the DNA dependent RNA polymerase is a holoenzyme (α₂ββ'ω σ) responsible for initiation, elongation and termination during transcription. DNase degrades DNA. DNA dependent DNA polymerase is involved in replication. DNA ligase joins DNA fragments.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Receptors for sperm binding in mammals are present on:
questions.solution_text: Zona pellucida has receptors for sperm binding (ZP3 receptors) in mammals. Corona radiata is a layer of radially arranged cells of membrana granulosa. Perivitelline space lies between vitelline membrane and zona pellucida.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The centriole undergoes duplication during:
questions.solution_text: During S phase, DNA replication takes place. In animal cells, centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm during S phase. G2 phase involves duplication of mitochondria, chloroplast and Golgi bodies.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which one of the following organisms bears hollow and pneumatic long bones?
questions.solution_text: Hollow and pneumatic long bones are present in class Aves. Neophron (vulture) belongs to class Aves. Ornithorhynchus (Platypus) and Macropus (Kangaroo) = Mammalia. Hemidactylus (wall lizard) = Reptilia.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Erythropoietin hormone which stimulates R.B.C. formation is produced by:
questions.solution_text: Juxtaglomerular (JG) cells of kidney secrete erythropoietin, which stimulates RBC formation. Alpha cells of pancreas produce glucagon. Rostral adenohypophysis cells synthesize anterior pituitary hormones.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Match the following: (a) Physalia, (b) Limulus, (c) Ancylostoma, (d) Pinctada — (i) Pearl oyster, (ii) Portuguese Man of War, (iii) Living fossil, (iv) Hookworm
questions.solution_text: Physalia: Portuguese Man of War (ii). Limulus: living fossil / king crab (iii). Ancylostoma: hookworm (iv). Pinctada: pearl oyster (i).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: During the process of gene amplification using PCR, if very high temperature is not maintained in the beginning, then which of the following steps of PCR will be affected first?
questions.solution_text: High temperature (~94°C) is required for denaturation, which is the first step of PCR. If high temperature is not maintained at the beginning, denaturation will be affected first.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements wrongly represents the nature of smooth muscle?

options.text: Communication among the cells is performed by intercalated discs
These muscles are present in the wall of blood vessels

questions.solution_text: Intercalated discs are found only in cardiac muscle tissue, not in smooth muscle. Smooth muscle fibres are non-striated and involuntary, present in walls of blood vessels, uterus, gall bladder and alimentary canal.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The organelles that are included in the endomembrane system are

options.text: Endoplasmic reticulum, Mitochondria, Ribosomes and Lysosomes
Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, Lysosomes and Vacuoles
Golgi complex, Mitochondria, Ribosomes and Lysosomes
Golgi complex, Endoplasmic reticulum, Mitochondria and Lysosomes

questions.solution_text: Endomembrane system consists of ER, Golgi complex, vacuoles and lysosomes. Mitochondria is a semi-autonomous organelle (excluded). Ribosomes are non-membranous (excluded).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Aspergillus niger, (b) Acetobacter aceti, (c) Clostridium butylicum, (d) Lactobacillus — (i) Acetic Acid, (ii) Lactic Acid, (iii) Citric Acid, (iv) Butyric Acid
questions.solution_text: Aspergillus niger → citric acid (iii). Acetobacter aceti → acetic acid (i). Clostridium butylicum → butyric acid (iv). Lactobacillus → lactic acid (ii).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: For effective treatment of the disease, early diagnosis and understanding its pathophysiology is very important. Which of the following molecular diagnostic techniques is very useful for early detection?
questions.solution_text: ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay) is used for early detection by detecting pathogenic antigens or antibodies. Southern blotting detects specific DNA sequences. Western blotting detects specific proteins. (Note: Both options 2 and 3 were accepted as correct by the official answer key.)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Digestive System and Anatomy of Cockroach
questions.question_text: Which of the following characteristics is incorrect with respect to cockroach?

options.text: A ring of gastric caeca is present at the junction of midgut and hind gut
Hypopharynx lies within the cavity enclosed by the mouth parts
In females, 7th-9th sterna together form a genital pouch
10th abdominal segment in both sexes, bears a pair of anal cerci

questions.solution_text: A ring of gastric caecae is present at the junction of foregut and midgut, not midgut and hindgut. At the junction of midgut and hindgut, malpighian tubules are present.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Persons with 'AB' blood group are called as 'Universal recipients'. This is due to:

options.text: Absence of antigens A and B on the surface of RBCs
Absence of antigens A and B in plasma
Presence of antibodies, anti-A and anti-B, on RBCs
Absence of antibodies, anti-A and anti-B, in plasma

questions.solution_text: AB blood group individuals contain antigens A and B on RBCs but lack antibodies anti-A and anti-B in plasma. Because they have no antibodies to react with donated blood, they can accept blood from all groups — hence 'universal recipients'.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Dobson units are used to measure thickness of:
questions.solution_text: The thickness of ozone in a column of air from the ground to the top of atmosphere is measured in Dobson units (1 DU = 1 ppb). CFCs are ozone depleting substances. The lowermost atmospheric layer is troposphere; ozone is in the stratosphere.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Read the following statements: (a) Metagenesis is observed in Helminths. (b) Echinoderms are triploblastic and coelomate animals. (c) Round worms have organ-system level of body organization. (d) Comb plates present in ctenophores help in digestion. (e) Water vascular system is characteristic of Echinoderms. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution_text: (a) Incorrect — metagenesis is in Coelenterata (Cnidaria), not helminths. (b) Correct — Echinoderms are triploblastic and coelomate. (c) Correct — Roundworms (Aschelminths) have organ system level. (d) Incorrect — comb plates help in locomotion. (e) Correct — water vascular system is in Echinoderms.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a cross between a male and female, both heterozygous for sickle cell anaemia gene, what percentage of the progeny will be diseased?
questions.solution_text: Cross: HbA HbS × HbA HbS → HbS HbS (25%), HbA HbS (50%), HbA HbA (25%). Only HbS HbS individuals are diseased = 25%.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which enzyme is responsible for the conversion of inactive fibrinogens to fibrins?
questions.solution_text: Thrombokinase helps convert prothrombin to thrombin. Thrombin then converts inactive fibrinogen to fibrin threads, which form the clot. Renin converts angiotensinogen to angiotensin-I. Epinephrine is secreted by adrenal medulla in stress responses.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Select the favourable conditions required for the formation of oxyhaemoglobin at the alveoli.

options.text: High pO2, low pCO2, less H+, lower temperature
Low pO2, high pCO2, more H+, higher temperature
High pO2, high pCO2, less H+, higher temperature
Low pO2, low pCO2, more H+, higher temperature

questions.solution_text: Oxyhaemoglobin formation at alveoli requires: high pO2, low pCO2, less H+ and lower temperature. Dissociation of oxyhaemoglobin at tissues requires: low pO2, high pCO2, high H+ and high temperature.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Sphincter of oddi is present at:

options.text: Junction of hepato-pancreatic duct and duodenum

questions.solution_text: The bile duct and pancreatic duct open into the duodenum as the hepato-pancreatic duct, guarded by the sphincter of Oddi. Ileo-caecal valve prevents backflow of faecal matter. Gastro-oesophageal sphincter regulates oesophagus-stomach opening.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which stage of meiotic prophase shows terminalisation of chiasmata as its distinctive feature?
questions.solution_text: Chiasmata (X-shaped structures) form in diplotene stage and terminalise in diakinesis. Bivalents form in zygotene. Crossing over occurs in pachytene. Chromosomal compaction starts in leptotene.

questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an objective of Biofortification in crops?
questions.solution_text: Biofortification improves vitamin content, protein content and micronutrient and mineral content of crops. It does not aim to create disease resistance in plants.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The partial pressures (in mm Hg) of oxygen (O2) and carbon dioxide (CO2) at alveoli (the site of diffusion) are:
questions.solution_text: At alveoli: pO2 = 104 mm Hg, pCO2 = 40 mm Hg. Atmosphere: pO2 = 159, pCO2 = 0.3. Deoxygenated blood: pO2 = 40, pCO2 = 45. Oxygenated blood: pO2 = 95, pCO2 = 40.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Veneral diseases can spread through: (a) Using sterile needles (b) Transfusion of blood from infected person (c) Infected mother to foetus (d) Kissing (e) Inheritance
questions.solution_text: STDs can spread through transfusion of blood from infected person (b) and from infected mother to foetus (c). They are NOT transmitted through kissing or inheritance. Sterile needles do not transmit infection.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A specific recognition sequence identified by endonucleases to make cuts at specific positions within the DNA is:
questions.solution_text: Each restriction endonuclease recognizes a specific palindromic nucleotide sequence in DNA and cuts both strands. Okazaki fragments are in DNA replication. Poly(A) tail is added at 3' end of hnRNA. Degenerate primers have multiple possible bases at some positions.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements about Histones is wrong?

options.text: Histones are organized to form a unit of 8 molecules
The pH of histones is slightly acidic
Histones are rich in amino acids - Lysine and Arginine
Histones carry positive charge in the side chain

questions.solution_text: Histones are rich in basic amino acid residues lysine and arginine with positively charged side chains. Their pH is basic (not acidic). Four types (H2A, H2B, H3, H4) occur in pairs to produce a histone octamer (8 molecules).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: During muscular contraction which of the following events occur? (a) 'H' zone disappears (b) 'A' band widens (c) 'I' band reduces in width (d) Myosine hydrolyzes ATP, releasing the ADP and Pi. (e) Z-lines attached to actins are pulled inwards.
questions.solution_text: During muscle contraction: H zone narrows/disappears, I band reduces, Z lines are pulled inwards, and myosin hydrolyzes ATP. The A band length remains constant (does NOT widen). So (b) is wrong; (a), (c), (d), (e) are correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Scapula, (b) Cranium, (c) Sternum, (d) Vertebral column — (i) Cartilaginous joints, (ii) Flat bone, (iii) Fibrous joints, (iv) Triangular flat bone
questions.solution_text: Scapula: large triangular flat bone (iv). Cranium: flat skull bones joined by fibrous sutures/fibrous joints (iii). Sternum: flat bone on ventral midline (ii). Vertebral column: adjacent vertebrae joined by cartilaginous joints allowing limited movement (i).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of these is not an important component of initiation of parturition in humans?

options.text: Increase in estrogen and progesterone ratio

questions.solution_text: Parturition involves: estrogen/progesterone ratio increase, prostaglandins (stimulate uterine contractions) and oxytocin (birth hormone, causes strong uterine contractions). Prolactin is a lactation hormone with no role in initiating parturition.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Assertion (A): A person goes to high altitude and experiences 'altitude sickness' with symptoms like breathing difficulty and heart palpitations. Reason (R): Due to low atmospheric pressure at high altitude, the body does not get sufficient oxygen.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution_text: Altitude sickness occurs at high altitude because low atmospheric pressure reduces oxygen availability, causing nausea, fatigue and heart palpitations. (R) correctly explains (A).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Following are the statements with reference to 'lipids'. (a) Lipids having only single bonds are called unsaturated fatty acids. (b) Lecithin is a phospholipid. (c) Trihydroxy propane is glycerol. (d) Palmitic acid has 20 carbon atoms including carboxyl carbon. (e) Arachidonic acid has 16 carbon atoms. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution_text: (a) Incorrect — single bond lipids are saturated; unsaturated have C=C double bonds. (b) Correct — Lecithin is a phospholipid. (c) Correct — Glycerol = trihydroxy propane. (d) Incorrect — Palmitic acid has 16 carbons. (e) Incorrect — Arachidonic acid has 20 carbons.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The Adenosine deaminase deficiency results into
questions.solution_text: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) enzyme is crucial for the immune system to function. Its deficiency results in dysfunction of the immune system. Addison's disease: hyposecretion of adrenal cortex hormones. Parkinson's: CNS degenerative disorder.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following secretes the hormone, relaxin, during the later phase of pregnancy?
questions.solution_text: Relaxin is produced by the corpus luteum (ruptured Graafian follicle with endocrine function) in the later phase of pregnancy. Graafian follicle is not formed during pregnancy. Uterus and foetus do not produce relaxin.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Identify the types of cell junctions that help to stop the leakage of the substances across a tissue and facilitation of communication with neighbouring cells via rapid transfer of ions and molecules.

options.text: Gap junctions and Adhering junctions, respectively
Tight junctions and Gap junctions, respectively
Adhering junctions and Tight junctions, respectively.
Adhering junctions and Gap junctions, respectively

questions.solution_text: Tight junctions stop leakage of substances across a tissue. Gap junctions (communication junctions) facilitate communication between cells by connecting cytoplasm of adjoining cells for rapid transfer of ions and molecules.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a step in Multiple Ovulation Embryo Transfer Technology (MOET)?

options.text: Cow is administered hormone having LH like activity for super ovulation
Cow yields about 6-8 eggs at a time
Cow is fertilized by artificial insemination
Fertilized eggs are transferred to surrogate mothers at 8-32 cell stage

questions.solution_text: In MOET, cows are administered hormones with FSH-like activity (not LH-like) for superovulation. 6-8 eggs per cycle are produced, the cow is fertilized by artificial insemination, and 8-32 celled embryos are transferred to surrogate mothers.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Filariasis, (b) Amoebiasis, (c) Pneumonia, (d) Ringworm — (i) Haemophilus influenzae, (ii) Trichophyton, (iii) Wuchereria bancrofti, (iv) Entamoeba histolytica
questions.solution_text: Filariasis: Wuchereria bancrofti (iii). Amoebiasis: Entamoeba histolytica (iv). Pneumonia: Haemophilus influenzae (i). Ringworm: Trichophyton (ii).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Allen's Rule and Types of Adaptation
questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Allen's Rule, (b) Physiological adaptation, (c) Behavioural adaptation, (d) Biochemical adaptation — (i) Kangaroo rat, (ii) Desert lizard, (iii) Marine fish at depth, (iv) Polar seal
questions.solution_text: Allen's Rule: Polar seal (shorter extremities to minimize heat loss) (iv). Physiological adaptation: Kangaroo rat (i). Behavioural adaptation: Desert lizard (manages body temp through behaviour) (ii). Biochemical adaptation: Marine fish at depth (iii).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Adaptive radiation, (b) Convergent evolution, (c) Divergent evolution, (d) Evolution by anthropogenic action — (i) Selection of resistant varieties due to excessive use of herbicides and pesticides, (ii) Bones of forelimbs in Man and Whale, (iii) Wings of Butterfly and Bird, (iv) Darwin Finches
questions.solution_text: Adaptive radiation: Darwin's finches (iv). Convergent evolution: Wings of butterfly and bird (analogous organs, similar function) (iii). Divergent evolution: Bones of forelimbs in man and whale (homologous organs) (ii). Anthropogenic: herbicide/pesticide resistant varieties (i).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Statement I: The codon 'AUG' codes for methionine and phenylalanine. Statement II: 'AAA' and 'AAG' both codons code for the amino acid lysine.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true

questions.solution_text: AUG codes for methionine only and acts as initiator codon — it does NOT code for phenylalanine (Statement I is incorrect). Both AAA and AAG code for lysine — this shows degeneracy of the genetic code (Statement II is correct).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Following are the statements about prostomium of earthworm. (a) It serves as a covering for mouth. (b) It helps to open cracks in the soil into which it can crawl. (c) It is one of the sensory structures. (d) It is the first body segment. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution_text: (a) Correct — prostomium covers the mouth. (b) Correct — acts as a wedge to force open cracks in soil. (c) Correct — has receptors, so it is sensory. (d) Incorrect — the first body segment of earthworm is the peristomium, not prostomium.
